newsitem.title: USA: CSX Corp Q4 earnings rise but revs about.
newsitem.headline: CSX Corp Q4 earnings rise but revs about.

text.p: (Millions of Dollars, Except Per Share Amounts)
NOTE: Fourth quarter earnings rose compared to the year-ago quarter excluding a gain in the year-ago quarter of $51 million.

During the second quarter of 1995, the company recorded a $257 million pretax charge to recognize the estimated costs of initiatives to revise, restructure and consolidate specific operations and administrative functions at its rail and container-shipping units. The restructuring charge reduced net earnings for 1995 by $160 million, 76 cents per share.

In the fourth quarter of 1995, the company recognized a net investment gain of $77 million, $51 million after-tax, 24 cents per share, on the issuance of an equity interest in a Sea-Land terminal and related operations in Asia and the write-down of various investments.

On Aug. 1, 1996, the company issued approximately 5 million shares of common stock to eligible officers and key employees under the terms of the amendment and restatement of the 1991 Stock Purchase and Loan Plan approved by the company's shareholders in April 1996. This resulted in an increase in average shares outstanding of 5 million and 2 million for the fourth quarter and year ended Dec. 27, 1996, respectively.

On Nov. 20, 1996, CSX acquired approximately 19.9 percent of the outstanding Conrail Common and Conrail ESOP Preferred Stock ("Conrail Shares") for $1.965 billion in cash, $110 per Conrail Share, pursuant to a merger agreement between the companies dated Oct. 14, 1996, as subsequently amended. The Conrail Shares were acquired with borrowings obtained under a bank credit facility negotiated by CSX subsequent to the announcement of the merger. In accordance with the merger agreement, the companies intend for CSX to acquire an additional 20.1 percent of Conrail Shares for cash at $110 per share. The remaining Conrail Shares will be acquired by CSX for a combination of 1.85619 shares of CSX Common Stock and CSX convertible preferred stock valued at $16 in exchange for each Conrail Share. In order for CSX to acquire additional Conrail Shares, Conrail (NYSE: CRR) shareholders must vote to opt- out of a Pennsylvania statute precluding CSX from owning 20 percent or more of Conrail. A competing hostile bid for the acquisition of Conrail has been offered by Norfolk Southern Corporation. The Conrail Shares acquired by CSX through the transactions described above will be placed in a voting trust pending the outcome of regulatory review of the transaction by the Surface Transportation Board.
